accepted.s: The National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI) was originally established at Bengaluru in 1923 and shifted to which place in 1955?
accepted.x: NDRI was established at Bengaluru in 1923 and shifted to Karnal in 1955.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional history and distinguish the original location from the later headquarters.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s: The Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), popularly known as the Pusa Institute, was established at Pusa, Bihar, in 1905 and shifted to which place in 1936?
accepted.x: IARI was established at Pusa in Bihar in 1905 and shifted to New Delhi in 1936.
accepted.tq: Track the chronological movement of an institution rather than selecting its founding location.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (CRIDA) is located at Hyderabad. The NRC on Camel is at Bikaner, NRC on Seed Spices at Ajmer and NRCWA at Bhubaneswar.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure institutional-location pair and eliminate swapped locations.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about ICAR institutes:
1. The Central Rice Research Institute is located at Cuttack.
2. The Central Tobacco Research Institute is located at Rajahmundry in Andhra Pradesh.
3. The National Research Centre on Camel is located at Bikaner.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: CRRI is at Cuttack, CTRI at Rajahmundry and the NRC on Camel at Bikaner.
accepted.tq: Verify each location independently before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s:
Arrange the following ICAR institutions in chronological order of the years given for their establishment:
A. IARI
B. NDRI
C. CRRI
D. CTRI
accepted.x: The order is IARI (1905), NDRI (1923), CRRI (1946) and CTRI (1947).
accepted.tq: Arrange the institutions by their establishment years, beginning with the earliest.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s: Which one of the following ICAR institutions was established in 2000?
o: Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture
National Research Centre on Seed Spices
National Research Centre for Women in Agriculture
accepted.x: The National Research Centre on Seed Spices was established in 2000.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its distinctive establishment year.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research was established in 1929 as an autonomous body under which department?
o: Department of Agricultural Research and Education
accepted.x: ICAR was established in 1929 and functions as an autonomous body under the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE).
accepted.tq: Use the parent-department trap by distinguishing DARE from similarly named scientific departments.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the structure of ICAR:
1. It has 72 research institutes.
2. It has 6 national bureaux.
3. It has 12 national research centres.
4. It has 22 directorates or Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The stated ICAR structure includes 72 research institutes, 6 national bureaux, 12 NRCs and 22 directorates/ATARIs.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical component separately before choosing the aggregate option.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s: As part of the plan mentioned for September 2026, how many priority Krishi Vigyan Kendras are proposed to be upgraded by March 2027?
accepted.x: The plan proposes upgrading 300 priority KVKs by March 2027.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact target figure and distinguish it from the other KVK-related numbers.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Krishi Vigyan Kendras?
o: They are state-level centres funded entirely by State Governments under DAE.
They are district-level centres administered by ICMR under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
They are privately funded agricultural laboratories outside the ICAR system.
They are district-level centres, 100% centrally funded under ICAR, and each comes under one of 11 ATARIs.
accepted.x: KVKs are district-level, 100% centrally funded under ICAR, and each functions under one of 11 ATARIs.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-structure clues to reject the wrong ministry and funding arrangements.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s: Unjha, located in Mehsana district, is noted for being which of the following?
accepted.x: Unjha in Mehsana, Gujarat, is Asia's largest seed-spice trading hub.
accepted.tq: Link the distinctive place-name with its specialised agricultural commodity trade.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s: Approximately what share of seed-spice exports is associated with Gujarat?
accepted.x: Gujarat accounts for approximately 80% of seed-spice exports.
accepted.tq: Use the percentage as the decisive quantitative clue.
accepted.sec: ICAR institutes → location, founding year; first Krishi Vigyan Kendra

accepted.s: The Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE) functions as an autonomous council under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
accepted.x: ICFRE is an autonomous council under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).
accepted.tq: Identify the correct parent ministry instead of a neighbouring science or agriculture ministry.
accepted.sec: ICFRE - founding year, headquarters, institutes → location

o: Institute of Forest Genetics and Tree Breeding — Coimbatore
Institute of Wood Science and Technology — Bengaluru
accepted.x: The Institute of Forest Biodiversity is located at Hyderabad, not Jabalpur. The Tropical Forest Research Institute is located at Jabalpur.
accepted.tq: Find the single swapped location among closely related forestry institutes.
accepted.sec: ICFRE - founding year, headquarters, institutes → location

accepted.s: The Department of Atomic Energy was established in 1954 by which means?
o: A resolution of the Planning Commission
An Act of Parliament passed in 1962
An executive order of the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board
accepted.x: DAE was established in 1954 by a Presidential Order. Its powers derive from the Atomic Energy Act, 1962.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the mode of establishment from the later statutory source of powers.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: The Department of Atomic Energy functions directly under the authority of the:
accepted.x: The Department of Atomic Energy functions directly under the Prime Minister.
accepted.tq: Apply the who-would-do-this-job approach to identify the supervising authority.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the principal function of the Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research?
o: Exploration of atomic minerals such as uranium and thorium
Regulation of nuclear and radiation safety
accepted.x: AMD undertakes exploration of atomic minerals, including uranium and thorium.
accepted.tq: Match the specialised unit with its distinctive function rather than a related nuclear activity.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about units associated with the Department of Atomic Energy:
1. The Heavy Water Board produces heavy water used as a moderator or coolant.
2. IREL deals with beach-sand minerals and rare earths such as monazite and ilmenite.
3. AERB is the regulator for nuclear and radiation safety.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Heavy Water Board produces heavy water, IREL handles beach-sand minerals and rare earths, and AERB regulates nuclear and radiation safety.
accepted.tq: Separate production, mineral-resource and regulatory functions before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: IGCAR — fast breeder reactor research and development
NPCIL — exploration of uranium and thorium
IREL — operation of nuclear power reactors
accepted.x: IGCAR at Kalpakkam undertakes fast breeder reactor research and development. The other functions belong to AMD, the Heavy Water Board and NPCIL respectively.
accepted.tq: Use the function-based elimination method and watch for swapped institutional roles.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: The Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) is primarily responsible for:
o: Building and operating nuclear power plants
accepted.x: NPCIL is a public sector undertaking that builds and operates nuclear power plants.
accepted.tq: Identify the operational agency from the activity described in the question.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre began in 1954 as the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay, and was renamed in 1967 after:
accepted.x: AEET was renamed Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in 1967 in honour of Homi Jehangir Bhabha.
accepted.tq: Use the renamed-in-honour-of relationship to distinguish prominent Indian scientists.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about BARC reactors is correct?
o: KAMINI is the only reactor among them fuelled by uranium-233.
APSARA was commissioned as the largest reactor in the BARC group.
Dhruva was Asia's first research reactor.
CIRUS is a 40 MW reactor that is still operating.
accepted.x: KAMINI is the only U-233-fuelled reactor in the listed group. APSARA was Asia's first research reactor, Dhruva is the largest, and CIRUS was shut down in 2010.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among reactors by fuel, size, chronology and operating status.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: APSARA, associated with BARC, is notable as:
o: The only U-233-fuelled reactor in India
The largest nuclear reactor in India
accepted.x: APSARA became critical in 1956 and is recognised as Asia's first research reactor.
accepted.tq: Match the reactor with its unique superlative rather than its fuel type or size.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: APSARA was Asia's first research reactor, not a fast breeder reactor. Dhruva, CIRUS and KAMINI are correctly matched as stated.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong reactor description by comparing unique identifying features.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: Which of the following BARC or DAE products is correctly matched with its use or description?
accepted.x: Bhabhatron is a cobalt therapy unit. Nisargruna is a biogas plant, AKRUTI is a rural incubator and TAG refers to groundnut varieties.
accepted.tq: Match each product to its specific application and reject cross-domain substitutions.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: Food irradiation associated with BARC/DAE enables potatoes and onions to be kept for approximately:
accepted.x: Food irradiation is used to preserve potatoes and onions for about eight months; the programme includes 25 irradiators.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive preservation duration as the quantitative clue.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: The AkRUTI rural incubator was developed in which year?
accepted.x: The AKRUTI rural incubator is a BARC/DAE product developed in 2007.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact year associated with the named technology rather than its institutional parent.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), established in 1945 at Bombay, is associated with which development?
o: The production of rare earth minerals
The establishment of district-level agricultural extension centres
The beginning of organised nuclear research in India
accepted.x: TIFR was established in 1945 at Bombay and marked the beginning of organised nuclear research in India.
accepted.tq: Connect the institution with its historical role rather than a later operational function.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: NCRA-TIFR operates the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope near which place?
accepted.x: NCRA-TIFR operates the GMRT near Pune.
accepted.tq: Use the location-specific institutional association while avoiding confusion with nuclear centres.
accepted.sec: DAE units → function; BARC products

accepted.s: As stated for the NPCIL fleet, which combination is correct?
o: 25 reactors, 8,480 MW; 10 reactors under construction with 8,500 MW
23 reactors, 7,500 MW; 9 reactors under construction with 7,480 MW
20 reactors, 6,480 MW; 7 reactors under construction with 5,500 MW
23 reactors, 7,480 MW; 9 reactors under construction with 7,500 MW
accepted.x: The stated NPCIL fleet comprises 23 reactors with 7,480 MW, while 9 reactors totalling 7,500 MW were under construction.

accepted.s: According to the stated NIRF 2025 rankings, Homi Bhabha National Institute stood at which positions?
o: 7th among research institutions, 12th among universities and 20th overall
12th among research institutions, 7th among universities and 20th overall
7th among universities, 20th among research institutions and 12th overall
20th among research institutions, 12th among universities and 7th overall
accepted.x: HBNI was ranked 7th among research institutions, 12th among universities and 20th overall in the stated NIRF 2025 rankings.

accepted.s: The Indian Council of Medical Research is the apex body for biomedical research under which parent department and ministry?
o: Department of Biotechnology, Ministry of Science and Technology
Department of Atomic Energy, Prime Minister's Office
Department of Agricultural Research and Education, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
accepted.x: ICMR functions under the Department of Health Research of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and is the apex body for biomedical research.
accepted.tq: Identify the parent department before considering the scientific field of the institution.
accepted.sec: ICMR - parent department, institutes → location, Vision 2030

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated foundations of ICMR's Strategic Plan and Vision 2030?
o: Alignment with the National Health Policy
Privatisation of all biomedical research institutions
accepted.x: The stated foundations are strengthening health research capacity, leveraging traditional medicine and aligning with the National Health Policy. Privatisation of all institutions is not included.
accepted.tq: Find the one extraneous policy objective among the three stated pillars.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent ICMR-related developments:
1. ICMR was restructured in 2026 into institute-led, priority-aligned research.
2. ICMR-SHINE 2nd edition is intended for Classes 9 to 12.
3. The draft National Health Research Policy, 2026, was released by the Department of Health Research.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 2026 restructuring was institute-led and priority-aligned, ICMR-SHINE targets Classes 9–12, and DHR released the draft National Health Research Policy, 2026.
accepted.tq: Check the year and responsible institution for each current-affairs statement.

accepted.s: ICMR-SHINE, in its second edition, is linked with which initiative?
accepted.x: The second edition of ICMR-SHINE for Classes 9–12 is linked with the initiative called “One Day as a Scientist”.
accepted.tq: Recognise the exact programme linkage rather than selecting a familiar health-sector mission.
